classification: Correctly implemented algebra; numerical discretization and tolerance are repository policies
bibliography: G. V. R. Rao, J. E. Beck, and T. E. Booth, Nozzle Optimization for Space-Based Vehicles, AIAA99-2584 (1999)
method: Original PDF pages rendered and inspected visually; no inference from damaged Markdown alone.
verdict: Signs and factors agree with source Eq5, obtained by eliminating dMstar/Mstar between source Eq2 and Eq3. Eq6 diagnostic also agrees algebraically.
source_requirement: For the advancing DE optimum-control-surface construction, a positive radial increment is required to continue; zero identifies its valid-region boundary.
numerical_policies: Segment midpoint theta,alpha,R discretization is a repository approximation; the source states finite increments without prescribing this exact averaging scheme.
Default tolerance1e-9 on normalized dR/R is a dimensionless repository boundary band, not a source-stated physical uncertainty or residual stopping tolerance.
Singular denominator cutoffs1e-14 and legacy Eq6 dtheta/difference cutoffs1e-12 are numerical policies.
Boundary_within_tolerance may include slight negative predicted increments within the declared band and is distinguished from strictly_positive.
applicability: Source Eq1 assumes fixed-length optimum-thrust stationarity along DE. Applying this test to a candidate is a local necessary construction diagnostic only.
It does not establish sufficiency, successful global BVP convergence, physical shock-free flow, exact D attachment, arbitrary fixed-exit-constraint optimality, or hardware qualification.
The sign of legacy Eq6b alone discards the other signed factors for arbitrary supplied segment orientation; direct Eq5 is the more explicit reported quantity.
Uniform axial theta=0 gives a singular0/0 reduction; unevaluable must not be relabeled as a shock or ordinary below-boundary evidence.
citation_correction: Eq2 and Eq3 are on PDFp3, not PDFp4; Eq5,Eq6 and boundary discussion are on PDFp4.
